title: Best Dehumidifier Humidifier Combo (2026) & How They Differ
h1: The Best Dehumidifier and Humidifier Combos — Plus the Real Difference Between Them
dek: Summer wants the water out; winter wants it back. Here's how to get year-round control without two machines fighting each other.
description: The best dehumidifier humidifier combo setups for 2026, from whole-house Aprilaire pairings to portable duos — plus the difference between the two machines.
intro: Shopping for a **dehumidifier humidifier combo** usually starts with a simple wish: one machine that keeps the house comfortable all year. Before you buy, it helps to know the difference between a dehumidifier and a humidifier, because they do exactly opposite jobs. A dehumidifier pulls water vapor *out* of the air to stop dampness, condensation and musty smells. A humidifier puts water vapor *into* the air to ease dry skin, static shocks and cracked wood in winter.

Here's the honest part: a single box that does both jobs well is rare. Most "2-in-1" listings turn out to be a dehumidifier with an air purifier bolted on, and the few true dual-mode units come from little-known brands with thin track records. What actually works is a *matched pair* — either two whole-house units run from one controller, or two portables set to targets that don't overlap. Below are the pieces we'd build that combo from, and how to set them up so they cooperate instead of compete.
topPicksLead: For a true set-it-and-forget-it combo, the **Aprilaire E100** paired with an Aprilaire 700 humidifier is the best whole-home setup; renters and single-room shoppers should pair a Midea Cube 35 with a Levoit OasisMist 450S.

products.name: Aprilaire 700 Fan-Powered Whole-House Humidifier
pros: Built-in fan, so no bypass duct is needed
Automatic control adjusts for outdoor temperature
One water panel per season is the main upkeep
cons: Needs a water line and drain at the furnace
Only works while the furnace blower runs
products.whyWeLoveIt: Winter is when a dehumidifier sits idle and the house dries out. The 700 is the winter half of the combo: it mounts on the furnace, adds moisture to the air going to every room, and its automatic control eases off on frigid nights so windows don't fog.
products.performance: Aprilaire rates it at up to about 18 gallons a day for homes up to roughly 4,200 square feet. Because it has its own fan, it doesn't need the extra bypass duct that the cheaper [Aprilaire](/best/best-aprilaire-dehumidifier/) 600 requires. Owners report the main chore is swapping the No. 35 water panel once a heating season, more often with hard water.

products.name: Honeywell HE280 Bypass Whole-House Humidifier
pros: Simple bypass design with few moving parts
Works with Honeywell Home humidity controls
cons: Needs a bypass duct between supply and return
Less output than a fan-powered or steam unit
products.whyWeLoveIt: If your furnace closet has room for a bypass duct, the HE280 is a lower-cost way to add the humidifying half of a whole-house combo. It's a familiar part to most HVAC techs, which keeps service simple.
products.performance: A bypass humidifier uses the furnace's own airflow to push air across a wetted pad, so there's no extra motor to fail. The trade-off is output: in a very large or leaky house it may not reach your winter target. Pair it with a ducted dehumidifier like the E100 or a [ducted dehumidifier](/best/best-ducted-dehumidifier/) from another brand for the summer half.

Use distilled or demineralized water if your tap water is hard, and see our [dehumidifier vs. humidifier](/guides/dehumidifier-vs-humidifier/) guide for when each one earns its keep.

sections.heading: What's the difference between a dehumidifier and a humidifier?

blocks.text: The short version: a dehumidifier removes moisture, a humidifier adds it. A typical compressor dehumidifier draws air across a cold coil, condenses water vapor into a tank or hose, and blows the drier air back out slightly warmer. A humidifier does the reverse — it evaporates, boils or atomizes water from a tank or water line into the room. Our deeper [dehumidifier vs. humidifier](/guides/dehumidifier-vs-humidifier/) guide covers health questions; here's the side-by-side.

sections.heading: How we pick dehumidifier and humidifier combos

blocks.text: We don't run a lab. We compared manufacturer ratings (pints per day under the 2019 DOE or AHAM test for dehumidifiers, gallons per day and coverage for humidifiers), ENERGY STAR listings, installation manuals and control compatibility, then read owner reviews for recurring failures — leaking reservoirs, sensors that drift, controls that let both machines run at once.
We left all-in-one units off because we couldn't find one from an established brand with published ratings for *both* functions.

sections.heading: What to look for in a humidifier and dehumidifier setup

items.label: A real humidistat on both machines
items.text: Each unit should stop at a set percentage. Fan-speed-only models can't share a room politely. Our [humidistat settings guide](/guides/dehumidifier-humidistat-settings-guide/) has seasonal targets.

items.label: A gap between the two targets
items.text: Set the dehumidifier to start around 50% and the humidifier to stop around 35–40%. That dead band keeps them from cycling against each other.

items.label: One controller, if you go whole-house
items.text: A thermostat or wall control that manages both — and locks out one while the other runs — is the single most important part of a ducted combo.

items.label: Right-sized capacity
items.text: Size the dehumidifier to your dampest space and the humidifier to your total heated square footage. A whole-house humidifier rated for a smaller home simply won't keep up.
sub: Whole home: a ducted dehumidifier plus a furnace-mounted humidifier
Single room: a 20–35 pint portable plus a 4–6 liter tabletop humidifier

items.label: Easy water handling
items.text: The dehumidifier needs somewhere to send water; the humidifier needs a steady supply. Plumbed whole-house units solve both; portables mean emptying one tank and filling another.

sections.heading: Is there a humidifier and dehumidifier in one?

blocks.text: A few exist, but they're harder to build well than they sound. Removing moisture takes a refrigeration circuit or a desiccant wheel; adding it takes a water reservoir and a wick, ultrasonic plate or heater. Cramming both into one portable cabinet means a small tank for each job and a lot of compromises, and the ones we found online come from little-known sellers with sparse specs.

items: **Dehumidifier + air purifier:** the most common 2-in-1. Useful in a damp, dusty room, but it can't add moisture. See our [dehumidifier and air purifier combo](/best/best-dehumidifier-air-purifier-combo/) guide.
**True dual-mode units:** rare, small and mostly from marketplace brands. Check the rated output for *each* mode before you trust the label.

blocks.title: Where real combos live
blocks.text: The genuine dehumidifier humidifier combo is a whole-house HVAC setup: a humidifier on the furnace and a ducted dehumidifier, both governed by one humidity control. That's the setup our top picks are built around.

sections.heading: Whole house humidifier and dehumidifier: how the pairing works

blocks.text: In a ducted home, the humidifier mounts on the furnace supply or return plenum and feeds moisture into heated air during winter. The dehumidifier connects to the return and supply ductwork (or a dedicated return) and dries air during the cooling season and shoulder months. A compatible thermostat or wall control watches indoor humidity and calls for whichever one is needed.

items: **Bypass (like the Honeywell HE280):** cheapest, simplest; needs a bypass duct and has the lowest output.
**Fan-powered (like the Aprilaire 700):** no bypass duct and more output; still relies on the furnace running.
**Steam:** highest output and works even when the furnace isn't heating; costs the most to buy and run.

blocks.text: Expect a licensed HVAC contractor for both halves, since each needs duct work, drain lines and low-voltage wiring. Our [whole-house dehumidifier installation](/guides/whole-house-dehumidifier-installation/) guide walks through what that job involves.

sections.heading: Running a portable humidifier and dehumidifier in one home

items: **Measure first.** Put a hygrometer in the room for a few days. If humidity sits between 35% and 50%, you may not need either machine running right now.
**Give each machine a season.** In most climates the dehumidifier runs from late spring to early fall and the humidifier from late fall through winter.
**Set non-overlapping targets.** Dehumidifier at 50%, humidifier at 35–40%. Never set them closer than about 10 points.

**Keep them apart if both must run.** In a split-level house, a damp basement may need a dehumidifier while an upstairs bedroom needs a humidifier — that's fine as long as they're in different zones with doors closed.

blocks.text: If you own a ducted home, the best dehumidifier humidifier combo is a matched pair — the **Aprilaire E100** for summer and the **Aprilaire 700** (or the budget **Honeywell HE280**) for winter — on one humidity control. In an apartment or single room, a **Midea Cube 35** plus a **Levoit OasisMist 450S** does the same job with a 10-point gap between their targets. Skip the all-in-one gadgets until a major brand makes one that's rated for both jobs.

faqs.q: What's the difference between a dehumidifier and a humidifier?
faqs.a: A dehumidifier removes moisture from the air to fix dampness, condensation and musty smells. A humidifier adds moisture to ease dry skin, static and dry sinuses. Most homes need a dehumidifier in humid months and a humidifier during heating season.

faqs.q: Is there a humidifier and dehumidifier in one?
faqs.a: A handful of dual-mode portables are sold online, mostly by little-known brands with limited specs for each mode. For dependable year-round control, a matched pair — either whole-house units on one control or two portables with separate targets — works better.

faqs.q: What is the best humidifier dehumidifier combo?
faqs.a: For a ducted home, the Aprilaire E100 dehumidifier paired with an Aprilaire 700 humidifier on a shared humidity control. For a single room or apartment, a Midea Cube 35 dehumidifier with a Levoit OasisMist 450S humidifier.

faqs.q: Can you run a humidifier and dehumidifier at the same time?
faqs.a: Not in the same room — they'll cancel each other out and waste power. In different zones of the house it can make sense, for example a dehumidifier in a damp basement and a humidifier in a dry upstairs bedroom.

faqs.q: Is a 2 in 1 air purifier and dehumidifier worth it?
faqs.a: It can be in a small, damp, dusty room, but it doesn't humidify, and most combos are modest on both jobs. In larger rooms a dedicated dehumidifier plus a separate HEPA purifier usually performs better.

faqs.q: Do I need a whole house humidifier and dehumidifier?
faqs.a: If your home regularly goes above 60% humidity in summer and below 30% in winter, and you have forced-air ductwork, a whole-house pair is the most hands-off solution. If only one or two rooms are a problem, portables are far cheaper.
